scope: Independent read-only chart, benchmark-research, release enrichment and public API review. No tracked files edited.

findings.finding: The initial chart resolver accepted source-checked numerical results despite unresolved evidence_concerns on their sources. This bypassed the existing stronger comparison gate.
findings.fix: Reject a curated panel if its sources or any resolved result/evaluation sources carry unresolved evidence concerns.
findings.verification: Source concern fixture now throws Comparison comparison: unresolved source concerns.

findings.finding: The initial resolver checked result status alone, allowing a currently checked result from a superseded evaluation to chart.
findings.fix: Reject missing or inactive evaluations and inactive protocol/dataset records.
findings.verification: Superseded evaluation fixture now throws Comparison comparison: inactive or missing evaluation. Protocol/dataset inactive checks also inspected.

findings.finding: The comparison gate initially did not require a finite numerical observation, so a null value with otherwise complete protocol metadata could be marked compatible.
findings.fix: Reject null, blank and nonfinite numerical values in compare; retain genuine N/A cells in a published table but omit them from plotted marks.
findings.verification: Null numeric compare returns compatible:false with explicit reason. Blank chart value throws. Latest component retains panel.rows in the evidence table and derives plotted rows by excluding null values.

findings.finding: Two results with identical required metadata but comparison.subset A versus B were accepted as compatible. The chart gate already rejected this difference, making the stronger API gate inconsistent.
findings.fix: Check subset whenever any selected row declares one; reject differing or partially unreported subsets while allowing all-absent optional subset metadata.
findings.verification: Same fixture now returns compatible:false and subset differs between evaluations.

successful_checks: Curated chart rows resolve directly from result IDs rather than results pagination; the 30-row regression verifies the last row and paper_compilation origin remain available.

Every chart metric/unit/direction and direct protocol/dataset association is checked. Suite/task roll-up requires a source-backed membership claim; a model used by a pipeline is not silently assigned pipeline results.

Panel source artifact SHA-256 is required. Source locators, reviewed grouping, exact printed values, origin and uncertainty remain exposed; missing compute/input parity does not get silently upgraded to automatic comparison compatibility.
Public source concerns and inactive result/evaluation/protocol/dataset conditions block charting after the fixes. Result history remains available without being eligible for chart marks.

Release IDs are explicit in router reads, client requests and responses. Cursors bind release and filters. The service serves a validated immutable release and checks the canonical serving snapshot against the release records digest.
The same recursive private-field denylist applies to query snapshots, schema validation and evidence indexes, including coverage and excluded records. Targeted privacy regressions passed.

Enrichment verifies reviewed record and overlay byte hashes, rejects duplicate/new unknown targets and unapproved overlay fields, and does not overwrite established metric directions. Historical release paths are separate from current additive enrichment.

Markup has a labeled select, section heading, figure caption, per-mark accessible names, captioned table with row/column headings, keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll region, and scope/uncertainty caveats. CSS wraps chart labels on narrow screens.

tests.outcome: All five negative scenarios rejected as intended after parent fixes.

limitations: This pass did not run a live browser, screen reader or narrow-viewport visual check; mobile layout/accessibility assertions are bounded to code and rendered static markup. Parent owns browser QA.
No live Firestore import/publication or emulator integration was executed in this pass; release consistency was read from the shared query, router, client and immutable service paths.

The standalone build validator accepts some Number-coercible non-decimal strings that service validation rejects. This pre-existing schema divergence is not exercised by reviewed decimal-string batches; harmonizing numeric grammar would prevent a future malformed release from building locally but failing service import.
